descs: Ash trees close in, gray on gray, and the trail keeps its own counsel.

spots.name: Widow's Well
spots.desc: A stone well, dry and capped with a warped board. Someone pried up one corner once and never set it right; a tarnished locket glints in the gap. East, the trees thin toward the barrow hill.

spots.name: The Last Trees
spots.desc: The ash wood thins to nothing. North the barrow hill rises, white grass on a bare slope and two stone doors set into it.
spots.brief: The last trees. The barrow north.

spots.name: Herb Hollow
spots.desc: A sunken hollow out of the wind. Wild herbs grow here, bitter but good for a wound — the only green in the whole gray wood. West the trees thin toward the barrow trail.

spots.name: Crow Perch
spots.desc: A blasted, leafless tree stands alone, hung with black feathers instead of leaves, rasping in the wind. A scrap of cloth is snagged high in the branches.

actions.label: climb for the scrap (grace, 1hp on fail)
fx: The branch holds. The scrap is fine-woven, gray, and stained dark with something old.
The branch bows and drops you back to the ash, empty-handed and scraped. It can be tried again.

spots.name: Gray Cairn
spots.desc: A cairn of flat stones older than the wood, the air over it gone cold and mineral. A gray husk crouches over the stones, guarding a river charm loose among them. It does not stir unless struck.
spots.brief: The gray cairn. The husk crouches.

actions.label: take the river charm from the cairn
fx: The charm comes free, and three old coins with it from under the stones.

spots.name: The Hollow Path
spots.desc: The ground dips into a sunken trail, root and stone rising to either side. Through a gap in the trees east, black water marks the sunken shrine; past it the watchtower's broken crown breaks the skyline.
spots.brief: The sunken trail. Shrine and tower east.

spots.name: Wolf Scrape
spots.desc: Claw marks score deep into an ash trunk, fresh enough to weep sap. A gaunt gray wolf watches from the scrub, ribs plain, and does not move first.
spots.brief: Clawed trunks. The gaunt wolf watches.

spots.name: Tower Shadow
spots.desc: The watchtower's shadow falls long across the path. Its stones rise east through the last trees. South, the ground drops toward black water.
spots.brief: Tower shadow. The tower stands east.

spots.name: Camp Smoke
spots.desc: A thread of smoke shows through the trees. The hunter's lean-to stands just beyond, to the west. North, a cairn of flat stones and a cold mineral smell.
spots.brief: Camp smoke. The camp lies west.

spots.name: The Ashfall Clearing
spots.desc: A wide clearing where the gray ash lies thickest, drifted like snow that never melts. East the ground softens and water glints; west a thread of woodsmoke rises.

actions.label: sift the ash where it lies thickest
fx: Under the gray, the ground is black and warm, as if something had burned here and never quite stopped. Your palm comes up clean. The gray is not soot; it never was.

spots.name: Twin Stones
spots.desc: Two standing stones lean together, worn faces touching. An ash wolf lies between them, gray coat gone to dust at the edges, watching you with a patience that is not a wolf's.
spots.brief: The leaning stones. The ash wolf watches.

spots.name: Sodden Verge
spots.desc: The ground turns soft and cold underfoot. East, black water glints through the trees where a stone roofline breaks the surface. A worn track climbs north toward the tower.
spots.brief: Soft ground. The shrine's water east.

spots.name: Broken Bridge
spots.desc: A footbridge half fallen into a dry streambed, the far rail gone. Woodsmoke drifts from the north. The village lanterns show through the trees east.

actions.label: search the dry streambed
fx: Under the fallen rail, a purse gone green with two coins still in it, and a child's wooden horse nobody came back for.

spots.name: The Split Oak
spots.desc: An oak split clean by old lightning at the wood's edge. East along the trail a lean wolf has taken the charcoal ring for its own; north the trail runs deeper; west, past a broken bridge, woodsmoke marks a hunter's camp.

spots.name: Charcoal Ring
spots.desc: A ring of blackened stone. Someone camped here and not recently — a boot-print in the ash, a tin cup on its side. A lean, blight-pale wolf crouches over the cold ash and lunges the moment it has your scent.

spots.name: Antler Stake
spots.desc: A stag's antlers lashed to a stake at the trail's edge click together in the wind — a marker, not a kill; strips of cloth are tied below, weathered past color. North the ground turns wet.

actions.label: look at the strips of cloth
fx: Old keeper-knots, the priest would call them. Someone marked the way to the sunken shrine for pilgrims, long before the pilgrims stopped.

va_hunters_camp.name: Hunter's Camp
va_hunters_camp.desc: A lean-to and a smoke rack at the wood's west edge, hides stretched to cure, herbs bundled to dry in the smoke. The hunter watches the trees, not you. A young woman in a hunter's leathers sits apart, fletching, and watches you instead.

variants.desc: A lean-to and a smoke rack at the wood's west edge, hides stretched to cure, herbs bundled to dry in the smoke. Two shapes work the rack now instead of one — Lys's brother, learning the smoke-cure again, badly, on purpose.
variants.brief: Lean-to and smoke. Two shapes at the rack now.

variants.desc: A lean-to and a smoke rack at the wood's west edge, hides stretched to cure, herbs bundled to dry in the smoke. The hunter watches the trees, not you. His son's bow-string hangs unused by the rack, waiting on a homecoming that hasn't come.
variants.brief: Lean-to and smoke. An unused bow-string waits.

actions.label: read the tally marks by the smoke rack
fx: Not idle scratches — a hunter's shorthand. A gap under a fallen stone on the barrow hill's north face, doors skipped entirely. Someone has been going in and out for years.
Scratches. A hunter's private shorthand; the hunter could read them for you.

actions.label: search the brush past the smoke rack
fx: Half-buried in old leaves: a tarnished clasp stamped with a rearing stag — the old king's mark, the same one on the elder's coffer lid — and two coins gone green.

va_drowned_chapel.name: Sunken Shrine
va_drowned_chapel.desc: Half a chapel, sunk to its windows in black water. A stone psalter stands above the waterline, its verses cut for a king who cannot rest. The wood lies west.

variants.brief: Black water. The water verse is yours.

actions.label: read the water verse (scholar)
fx: 'Let the water take what grief the living cannot; lay it down, and rest.' It comes back to you line by line, a scholar's ease. Water verse: known.

actions.label: trace the water verse by touch (grace)
fx: Your fingers find the worn grooves and trace them true. 'Let the water take what grief the living cannot; lay it down, and rest.' Water verse: known.
The grooves run together under your fingers. It can be tried again.

actions.label: work out the water verse (wits)
fx: The worn lines give up their meaning. 'Let the water take what grief the living cannot; lay it down, and rest.' Water verse: known.
The letters swim. It can be tried again.

va_watchtower.name: Old Watchtower
va_watchtower.desc: An old watchtower, stairs still sound. Wind carvings ring the bell room at the top. From the parapet the whole Vale lies gray below: village south, the barrow hill north-west, the fens east.

variants.brief: Wind in the bell room. The wind verse is yours.

actions.label: read the wind carvings (scholar)
fx: 'Let the wind take what iron could not; let it go, and rest.' The wind verse returns whole. Wind verse: known.

actions.label: trace the wind carvings by touch (grace)
fx: Quiet fingers find the wind-worn cuts. 'Let the wind take what iron could not; let it go, and rest.' Wind verse: known.
The wind has worn them too shallow for a first pass. It can be tried again.

actions.label: work out the wind carvings (wits)
fx: The carvings give up their meaning. 'Let the wind take what iron could not; let it go, and rest.' Wind verse: known.
The pattern will not hold still. It can be tried again.

actions.label: get your bearings from the parapet
fx: Your map, in words: the sunken shrine's water glints south of here; the barrow hill is the bare rise north-west past the last trees; the village lies south-west; the fens spread east, toward Hollowbrook.

va_river_charm.name: river charm
va_river_charm.hint: wards off harm just by riding in your pack

va_herbs.name: wild herbs
va_herbs.hint: eat them to heal a little

fx: Bitter, but they ease the ache.

va_herbs2.name: dried herbs
va_herbs2.hint: eat them to heal a little

fx: Bitter, but they ease the ache.
The clasp gives. Inside, a lock of hair gone gray and a name scratched into the tin: MAREN. Someone in the Reach will know it.

va_crow_scrap.name: faded scrap of cloth
va_crow_scrap.hint: fine-woven, watch gray, stained dark — worth showing the reeve

va_wolf_fang.name: ash-pale fang
va_wolf_fang.hint: pulled from the ash wolf — the hunter might want to see it

va_wolf_rib.name: gaunt rib-bone
va_wolf_rib.hint: pulled from the gaunt wolf — the hunter might want to see it

va_wolf_pelt.name: lean wolf's pelt
va_wolf_pelt.hint: the lean wolf's — the hunter might want to see it

va_hunter.name: hunter
va_hunter.desc: Long practice, out here alone with the wood pressing close.

topics.label: the wood
topics.say: Wolves gone gray and wrong. Keep moving and keep iron close. And mind the old king under that hill — kneel to him and he doesn't just take your life, he takes your place.

topics.label: the old barrow
topics.say: Doors face north, sealed since before me. There's a gap under a fallen stone on the north face if you'd rather not test the doors — it's in the tally by the rack. A verse is cut into the barrow's hall, too.

topics.label: herbs for the road
topics.say: Take them. Wolves run this wood and worse waits under the hill. Pay me by ending this.

topics.label: the young woman fletching
topics.say: Lys. Mine. Her brother went west to Thornwold to ride with the Free Company at Camp Gallows and hasn't sent word in a year. She'd go after him tomorrow if I let her. I don't. Ask her yourself; she'll tell you I'm wrong.

topics.label: show the ash wolf's fang
topics.say: That one circled my snares three nights running and never sprung one. Smarter than the rest of the gray. Good you ended it clean.
fx: The hunter presses a bundle of herbs and three coins into your hands.

topics.label: show the gaunt wolf's rib-bone
topics.say: Starving, that one — but starving things bite harder, not softer. Good you ended it clean.
fx: The hunter presses a bundle of herbs and three coins into your hands.

topics.label: show the lean wolf's pelt
topics.say: That's the one that jumped anyone who came near the old fire ring. Meanest of the three. Wood's quieter for it.
fx: The hunter presses a bundle of herbs and three coins into your hands.

topics.label: leave the hunter to the trees

va_ash_wolf.name: ash wolf
onDeath: The wolf drops. Its gray coat goes to dust. One fang holds its shape, ash-pale.
va_ash_wolf.desc: Gray to the bone and patient. It holds its ground and will let you pass if you let it be.

va_gaunt_wolf.name: gaunt wolf
onDeath: The gaunt wolf falls still, ribs plain through the gray coat. One rib comes away clean.

va_lean_wolf.name: lean wolf
onDeath: The lean wolf goes still, the last of the pack that watched the trail. Its pelt comes away thin as paper.

va_cairn_husk.name: gray husk
onDeath: The husk crumbles to gray dust over the stones. Whatever held it together came apart the night the barrow opened.
